newsitem.title: FRANCE: French envoy in belated meeting with Kabila.
newsitem.headline: French envoy in belated meeting with Kabila.

text.p: France's envoy to Kinshasa has met President Laurent Kabila of the Democratic Republic of Congo to voice concern over the safety of French nationals and the fate of refugees in the east of the nation, officials said on Monday.
The French Foreign Ministry said envoy Michel Rougagnou also raised the need to move towards free elections in the former Zaire and help in the region's security after months of civil war.
Rougagnou, who had been instructed 10 days ago to seek a meeting with the new ruler, was received on Sunday.
It was an indication of France's waning influence after it backed ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko that Kabila received the U.S. and British envoys before the French ambassador.
A senior French Foreign Ministry official visited Kinshasa last month but was not received by Kabila.
Paris had ordered its ambassador to demand protection for its nationals after the killing of two French businessmen in the capital shortly after the rebels seized power.
He was also instructed to express France's deep concern at the fate of refugees and demand that relief organisations and the United Nations be granted immediate access to the area.
France has repeatedly appealed for the security of hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees after reports of massacres by the Tutsi-led rebels.
It has also voiced concern that a ban on political activities in Kinshasa would hamper national reconciliation.
Kabila's administration has banned all political activities and public demonstrations in Kinshasa until further notice, citing a need to protect public security.
